title: Life experience and being ahead of the layman
summary: Hall says musicians meet all kinds of people and see life at every level.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: The question I wanted to raise was do you think that the ad lib player, the jazz player is more vulnerable to the put-on, the con, the promises of, hey, you're going to do this baby and, you know, and this, that and the other thing?
Well, that's the only thing that keeps you going, the expectation. Like, you know, it didn't happen today, but maybe it will tomorrow.
But you were saying also -- we were talking off mike -- that you feel the musicians such as yourself are ahead of the layman by, you know, and you were going on why --
Speaking about life, about life, not being a musician.
Yeah.
That span of -- mixing with people.
And you said you felt you were ten years ahead of the layman.
Right.
Because of what you see?
Because of what you experience. It's --
Well, I meant that.
It's like a prosty. She meets all sorts of people.
You see life all the time.
All the -- it's always there. It's always there in whatever, whatever level it is, and I've worked in dives, and I've worked for establishments, and it doesn't vary too much in between.
Huh. And you come into contact with people from all walks of life.
All walks of life.
So you get all kinds of trains of thought and lifestyles and what have you, friends.
I can meet -- I can meet John, Bill, Jack on the bandstand, who will leave me his card, but I have to go through his receptionist to see him in his office.
Uh-huh, yeah.
And that's the difference.
